subject: Materials Science
title: Semiconductor Lasers
description: A micro-lesson that makes Semiconductor Lasers usable.

hook.text: The laser in a Blu-ray player is a tiny semiconductor chip — smaller than a grain of sand, brighter than a lightbulb.

buildup.text: Stimulated emission in a direct band gap semiconductor produces coherent, monochromatic light.

discovery.text: Mirrors on two faces of the chip bounce photons back and forth, amplifying the light with each pass.

twist.text: Quantum well structures confine carriers in nanometer-thick layers — boosting efficiency and lowering threshold current.

climax.text: Fiber optic networks carrying internet traffic use InP laser diodes — each one pulsing billions of times per second.

punchline.text: A sliver of semiconductor smaller than a sand grain lights up the internet.

quiz.question: What do quantum wells do in semiconductor lasers?
options: They confine carriers in thin layers, improving efficiency
They filter out unwanted light wavelengths
